escalation.obstacle: Find a unit-distance graph with a genuine forced-equal distinct pair at k=5 (which by the corrected lemma requires chi>=5). Two seeds are now excluded by certificate. The open question is what structural feature makes the 5-colouring space rigid on a pair, given that richness of the colouring space defeated both seeds.
escalation.definitions: Unit-distance graph: finite graph with an injection into R^2 such that uv is an edge iff |u-v| = 1. Proper k-colouring: c(u) != c(v) on every edge. Forced equal at k: G is k-colourable and G plus the edge pq is not; the added edge is a combinatorial disequality constraint and is never a unit edge for a non-adjacent pair. Coordinates in Q(sqrt3,sqrt5,sqrt11), basis {1,3,5,11,15,33,55,165}, denominators dividing 288.
escalation.hypotheses: Exact real-algebraic coordinates; induced (all-pairs) edge set verified; k = 5; chi(G) >= 5 required for non-vacuity.
escalation.attempted_approaches: Common-neighbour palette excluders (Theorem B caps at 2 colours); clique-sum gluing (Theorem A); complete no-forcing certificates for H (553 vertices, 34 witnesses) and for H union (H+tau) (1048 vertices, 34 witnesses, 1048 unique signatures); adaptive equal-signature refinement driving survival sets to zero twice.
escalation.expected_useful_output: Either a forced-equal pair at k=5 with exact coordinates and a validated proof certificate, or a third seed that also resists, in which case the informative quantity is which invariant of the surviving classes differs between seeds; neither cross-edge count nor chromatic order has been shown to control rigidity.
